properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Anthony, 2026-08-09, describing what has already happened rather than a hypothetical.

THE SHAPE, in his numbering: projectA = **dynograph-foundation**, projectB = **reflow2**, projectC = **flo2**, projectD = **storyflow**. C depends on B; B depends on A; **D ALSO depends on A, and not on B.** A diamond, with A at the point. (projectE = embeddings-rs, and whether it is even a reflow2 project is undecided — recorded as unknown rather than assumed either way.)

⚠️ THE INCIDENT, WHICH IS THE EVIDENCE AND IS NOT HYPOTHETICAL. Anthony: \"projectB caused changes in projectA, which I implemented real time. **The risk was that the changes that projectB required on projectA might have caused issues with projectA now being able to support projectD** (I thought about it, but really didn't test that anything didn't break in projectD by using an updated projectA).\"

⇒ A change was levied UP one arm of the diamond and shipped, and **nothing checked the other arm.** The owner noticed the risk by thinking, and the check was never run. That is the failure mode, already realised, on the real projects.

=== WHY THIS IS NOT `dec:who-needs-to-know`, AND THE DIFFERENCE IS STRUCTURAL ===

That node asks whether notification is SUBSCRIBED or DERIVED from the blast radius, and prefers derived because `propagate_from` already computes who a change impacts. Its recorded counter-argument is: *\"a blast radius is only as good as the edges that exist, so an unrecorded dependency means a silent non-notification.\"*

**IN THE CROSS-GRAPH CASE THAT COUNTER STOPS BEING A RISK AND BECOMES A CERTAINTY.** The edge D→A lives in **D's graph**. A's graph does not hold it and cannot. So A's blast radius is not *possibly* incomplete — it is **NECESSARILY TRUNCATED AT THE GRAPH BOUNDARY**, every time, by construction. Derived notification cannot work from the upstream side, and no amount of edge hygiene in A fixes it.

⭐ AND IT IS THE SAME STRUCTURAL FACT `dec:idea-gap-flows-to-the-dependency` already turned on, pointing the other way. There, Anthony's Google-service argument defeated \"the upstream pulls\": a widely-depended-on design **cannot enumerate its dependents**. That killed pull for RECEIVING requirements. Here the identical fact kills push for SENDING warnings — A cannot warn D because A does not know D exists. **One fact, two directions, two different unbuildable mechanisms.** Which is a strong hint that the answer has to live on the CONSUMER side in both cases.

=== OPTIONS, NONE CHOSEN ===

**(A) THE CONSUMER MIRRORS AND NOTICES.** Each dependent mirrors the upstream's published surface and detects when the mirror drifts from the real one. **The machinery is already built and shipped** — `export_surface` (upstream publishes), `mirror_surface` / `mirrors` (consumer mirrors), `pair_designs`, `seam_report`. FOR: it scales exactly where push fails, because it needs no registry and no knowledge of who depends on you; each consumer looks after itself. It also inverts the burden onto the party who actually cares. COUNTER: it is a PULL, so it only fires when the consumer runs it — D learns it is broken when D next looks, not when A changes. For a project nobody has opened in three months, that is late.

**(B) A COMPOSITION RUN ACROSS ALL THE GRAPHS AT ONCE.** `compose_and_analyse` and `pair_designs` exist; `dec:linked-repos-poc` RAN this on reflow2 + flo2 + dynograph-foundation on 2026-08-06 and found \"the linking works, the labelling does not exist.\" **THAT BLOCKER HAS SINCE CLEARED** — reflow2 now declares 9 `required` interfaces, five of them pointed at dynograph (`ifc:req-dyno-*`). FOR: it computes the diamond directly — two consumers requiring the same interface means a change to it touches both — and Anthony HOLDS ALL FOUR GRAPHS, so it is runnable today. COUNTER: it needs somebody with every graph in hand, which is exactly the arrangement the Google-service argument says does not generalise. **Fine for the trial, not the answer.**

**(C) THE UPSTREAM KEEPS A REGISTRY OF ITS CONSUMERS.** FOR: A could then warn D. COUNTER: refuted twice already — registration is a write, so pull cannot bootstrap, and a heavily-depended-on design will not maintain it. Retained only for the small-federation case.

**(D) NOTHING MECHANICAL; THE OWNER REMEMBERS.** COUNTER: this is what happened, and the record above is what it cost — the risk was identified and the test still was not run. Not because anyone was careless, but because nothing made the omission visible afterwards.

=== THE FIRST TESTABLE STEP, WHICH COSTS ALMOST NOTHING ===

**Does storyflow (D) DECLARE its dependency on dynograph-foundation (A) as a `required` interface, the way reflow2 (B) now does?** reflow2's five `ifc:req-dyno-*` interfaces exist; whether D has any equivalent is UNKNOWN AND CHECKABLE. If it does not, no mechanism in any option above can work for D, and declaring it is the prerequisite for all of them. If it does, the diamond is already computable with tools that shipped.

📌 AND THE METHOD IS ANTHONY'S OWN, STATED THE SAME DAY: *\"the best development of reflow2 has been propose something — trial it with a real project — then learn from it — iterate upon the solution and try again.\"* These four projects are that trial, and the diamond is the first thing to run it on.

NOTHING IS PROMOTED.

═══ 2026-10-01 — @AJS: HOW WOULD "A CHANGE REACHES SIBLING REPOS ON ITS OWN" BE DELIVERED? (recorded as brainstorming; nothing chosen) ═══
Context: his workplace "project brain" deck lists it as still open: "today the hub's agent routes it and says where." His example is a beamline fix in xpdtools that should reach ophyd-async, ioc_host_vars, the profile collections and n2sndocs. dec:until-designs-share-a-server-the-cross-design-check-runs-at-the-hub (ACCEPTED) already settles that the cross-design check runs at the hub, read before any write. What is open is the ON ITS OWN part: nobody has to remember to ask.

DELIVERY OPTIONS:
(a) A SCHEDULED HUB CHECK. On a schedule, or on each merge, the hub reads each tracked design's changes since it last looked (upstream_status, sync_status, its own watch records). Where a change crosses into a sibling, it opens a PROPOSED item in that sibling: a question, gap or levied requirement (dec:idea-gap-flows-to-the-dependency), and says where.
(b) DECLARED SURFACES BETWEEN DESIGNS. Each design publishes what it provides, and its dependents mirror what they consume (mirror_surface, pair_designs, seam_report). A change to a provided surface then reaches its consumers through propagation, not through judgement.
(c) CI ON MERGE TRIGGERS (a) for the repo that merged, so the moment of change is the moment of notice.

🛑 THE COUNTER THAT BOUNDS ALL THREE: "on its own" must mean the sibling IS TOLD, never that it IS EDITED. A design's owner moves its intent, and flo2 settled that sharing a hub never shares its children. So an automatic change arrives as a proposed item its owner accepts or declines, never as a write. The blast radius is also only as good as the edges between repos, so (b) is the precondition for (a) being more than a guess.

SIZES: (a) medium, on existing hub machinery plus a scheduler. (b) medium-large: surfaces have to be declared per repo pair. (c) small once (a) exists.
properties.name: OPEN — when a change to a shared upstream is driven by one dependent, how does the OTHER dependent find out? (the diamond: B and D both depend on A, and A's blast radius stops at its own graph)
properties.rationale:
Captured under the brainstorm skill, and kept SEPARATE from two neighbours it would otherwise be merged into — a node holding two questions can only ever be half-answered. `dec:idea-gap-flows-to-the-dependency` is the UP direction (how a dependent levies a need on its upstream); this is the DOWN-AND-SIDEWAYS direction (how a change to a shared upstream reaches a sibling that never asked). `dec:who-needs-to-know` is the SAME-GRAPH version and prefers derived notification; the point of this node is that derivation is structurally impossible across a graph boundary, which that node's own counter-argument anticipates without naming the cross-graph case.

Recorded because the failure has already occurred on the real projects and was survived by luck rather than by a check — and because the prerequisite that blocked every mechanism (no labelled seam) cleared three days after it was written down.
